thread:
cara: Heads up — after the 03:00 canary rollout we started seeing a spike in 5xx/gateway timeouts for hosted inference customers. Some high-traffic routes are getting 502/504. Raising an incident, tagging eng-runtime and oncall.

mike: Seeing it in metrics now.  p50 latency up ~2x, p95 is timeout. 5xx rate jumped from 0.3% -> 6% across gateway-proxy cluster.

sasha: Got multiple customer escalations: errors are `502 Bad Gateway` and `504 Gateway Timeout` for API calls to /v1/generate. They report partial billing for requests that never returned.

lee: Any recent config flips or feature flags for auth/routing?

cara: Canary included two changes: auth proxy migration (auth_proxy_v2=true) and a routing trace header change. I suspect auth_proxy_v2.

jen: Confirming: deploy-bot shows the canary rollout started at 1865439600. It was a partial rollout (10% traffic) but routing policy changed to prefer canary for new connections.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout: service=api-gateway, version=2026.03.08-canary, traffic=10%, started=1865439600

mike: Logs show retries from gateway to auth-svc timing out. Example from gateway logs: 
```
<gateway> [WARN] upstream request failed: connect_timeout to auth.internal:443 after 30s, upstream_status=504
```

cara: Auth team, are you seeing increased latencies on auth-svc?

lee: Auth team reports no CPU/memory spike on auth pods, but connection success rate to auth-db has small increase in errors. Could be new TLS negotiation path in v2.

support-bot: Customer: @AcmeInc — 70 failing requests since 03:02; errors 502/504. Billing question escalated. Ticket #24567

sasha: Need immediate mitigation — revert the canary or shift traffic away. If the flag is causing gateway to open long-lived auth connections that hang, that would explain timeouts.

mike: I can flip routing weights back to 0% for canary. That should drain new sessions to canary. Suggest we do that asap and monitor 5xx.

cara: Agreed. mike — please coordinate with deploy-bot, and @jen please prepare rollback if weights flip doesn't help.

mike: Flipping weights now: `kubectl annotate svc api-gateway rollout-weight=0 --namespace=prod` (running)

deploy-bot: Adjusted rollout weight: service=api-gateway, version=2026.03.08-canary, traffic=0%

mike: Monitoring... 2 minutes in — 5xx rate trending down in front-end metrics. p95 latency returning to baseline.

jen: Good. Initiate graceful drain of canary pods and hold rollback plan as contingency.

cara: Support — please message the customers with a short blurb: we've paused canary and are investigating; they should see requests succeed now. Apologize and offer to adjust billing if they were impacted.

sasha: Sending message to customers now.

support-bot: Sent templated update to affected customers: "We paused the recent canary rollout at 03:05 UTC after detecting increased 5xx. Services are recovering; we're investigating and will follow up."

lee: For postmortem: initial hypothesis — auth_proxy_v2 introduces a new TLS handshake path that sometimes hangs when upstream auth-db responds slowly, causing long timeouts. Gateway treats upstream timeout as 504 and bubbles as 502 for some proxies. Need to trace connection lifecycles.

mike: Action items (short term): 1) keep canary weight at 0% until root cause identified; 2) add a shorter connect_timeout with circuit breaker on gateway->auth to fail fast; 3) rollback auth_proxy_v2 in next safe window if needed.

cara: I'll file an incident ticket and own coordination. jen/lee/mike — please add repro steps and logs to the ticket.

jen: Repro steps I ran locally: curl to gateway with canary header -> gateway proxies to auth v2 which stalls. Quick repro command: 
```
curl -v -H "X-Canary: canary" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```
Captured response: `HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout` and gateway log snippet above.

lee: I'll dig into auth-proxy code paths for TLS renegotiation and look for blocking calls.

sasha: Support note: customers asking about billing — we should coordinate refunds for failed-but-billed requests. cara, finance/sales must be pinged.

cara: @mike can you export a list of request IDs with 5xx and timestamps so finance can compute impact?

mike: Will dump logs and share S3 link in the incident ticket within 30m.

deploy-bot: Canary pods draining: 3 remaining -> 0

mike: Canary fully drained. Frontend 5xx back to baseline (0.4%).

cara: Great. For tomorrow: schedule a tabletop with eng-runtime, auth, and oncall to do a controlled replay and run the canary with additional observability (tcpdump, tls debug). Also add a short circuit-breaker policy on the gateway to avoid cascading timeouts.

lee: I'll add a telemetry patch to capture handshake durations for auth connections and a histogram of upstream connect times.

jen: And we should update the rollout checklist to include a canary-traffic-attenuation gate: ensure rollback route exists and that canary uses 0% sticky sessions by default.

cara: Filing post-incident follow-ups: 1) RC for billing adjustments; 2) code review for auth_proxy_v2 edge-case; 3) rollout checklist changes; 4) alert thresholds tuned to detect auth upstream latency increases before 5xx spike.

sasha: Thanks all. Closing slack thread when next steps are documented in the incident ticket. :thumbsup:
